title: GitHub - Zagitta/gpu-unlock: Unlock FP/BF16 instruction issue rate on Nvidia 3000's cards to their professional equivalents
html:
Unlock FP/BF16 instruction issue rate on Nvidia 3000's cards to their professional equivalents

This Linux kernel module combines the CMP unlocker's V67/PLM technique with the pre-driver timing of the UEFI approach. It runs the unlock, writes the speed selectors (SS0 

0x88888888
, which selects the full BF16 rate, and the 4-bit SS1 
0x8
IMLA4) and performs FLR before the unmodified NVIDIA driver binds the card. It is neither a UEFI application nor a patched NVIDIA driver.

The benefit of this early kmod driver is that it does not require manual patching each time nvidia releases a new driver version.

The effect of this unlock is that it doubles the instruction issuing speed of FP/BF16 FMA into FP32 operations on GA102, GA103, GA104 and GA106 cards.

3090 Ti dense 8192³ GEMM at 450 W, five-sample medians with FP32 accumulation:

Input Before After
FP16 87.46 TFLOPS 118.39 TFLOPS
BF16 87.50 TFLOPS 157.41 TFLOPS
TF32 42.58 TFLOPS 82.61 TFLOPS

Results reported by users. The module accepts every GeForce ID listed in 

kernel/gpu_unlock/main.c
, but the cards below are the ones someone has reported on. Please add yours with a compatibility report, whether it worked or not.

Chip Card PCI ID Result BF16 GEMM gain Reports
GA102RTX 3090 Ti
10de:2203
 Unlocked+68–80%#1
GA102RTX 3090
10de:2204
 Unlocked+25–67%#5, #9, #10, #17, #25, #27, #33
GA102RTX 3080 Ti 20 GB (OEM, GA102-250)
10de:2205
 Unlock completes, BF16 stays at half rate—#28
GA102RTX 3080 10 GB
10de:2206
 Unlocked+70–73%#14
GA102RTX 3080 20 GB (memory upgrade)
10de:2206
 Unlocked+56–59%#10, #15
GA104RTX 3070
10de:2484
 Unlocked+73–81%#10, #12
GA104RTX 3070 Ti
10de:2482
 Not tested with this module (the same unlock worked from a UEFI port on Windows)—#32
GA106RTX 3060 12 GB
10de:2504
 Unlockedabout +80%#13, #31
GA103any
10de:2414
 No reports yet——

The gains are dense GEMM throughput from each report's own benchmark, so they are not directly comparable. The power limit matters a lot: the lowest figure (+25%) is from cards capped at 225 W.

Matrix-heavy work speeds up: LLM prefill (+14–36% in #9, #15, #25 and #33), diffusion and FlashAttention. LLM decode, which is limited by memory bandwidth, and INT8 work stay about the same. The reports that compared outputs found them bit-identical before and after.

Reports also cover up to four cards in one machine, the card driving the display, and cards passed through to a VM with vfio-pci (#17).

First run:

git clone https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock
cd gpu-unlock
make install

Then append 

gpu_unlock.targets=all
to your kernel command line, keeping existing options:

  • GRUB (Debian/Ubuntu/Mint): add it inside 
    GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT
    in 
    /etc/default/grub
    , then run 
    sudo update-grub
    .
  • GRUB (Arch/CachyOS): same edit, then run 
    sudo grub-mkconfig -o /boot/grub/grub.cfg
    .
  • Fedora/RHEL: run 
    sudo grubby --update-kernel=ALL --args="gpu_unlock.targets=all"
    .
  • systemd-boot: append it to the 
    options
    line in your boot entry (
    bootctl status
    shows its location).
  • UKI / generated entries: add it to 
    /etc/kernel/cmdline
    and regenerate your boot images/entries (e.g. 
    sudo mkinitcpio -P
    for mkinitcpio UKIs).

Every build downloads the pinned NVIDIA/CachyOS inputs over HTTPS, checks their SHA-256, and generates firmware only in the build directory and the binary package. All three formats install through the same 

make install-*
targets. Packages are built from the committed 
HEAD
.

Build, install build dependencies, and install the packages in one step (asks for your sudo password):

make install        # detect the distribution and select an installer
make install-arch   # makepkg -sif
make install-deb    # apt-get build-dep, dpkg-buildpackage, apt-get install
make install-rpm    # dnf builddep, rpmbuild, dnf install

make install
uses 
/etc/os-release
(
ID
, then 
ID_LIKE
) to detect Arch, Debian/Ubuntu, or Fedora/RHEL/CentOS families. The RPM installer requires DNF. For other distributions, select a compatible explicit target above.

make arch
, 
make deb
and 
make rpm
only build. Debian and RPM packages go to 
build/deb
and 
build/rpm
. The NVIDIA inputs are cached in 
~/.cache/gpu-unlock/inputs
(
make inputs
; override with 
INPUTS=
). 
dpkg-buildpackage
itself never uses the network, so a clean-chroot build (sbuild or pbuilder) needs 
GPU_UNLOCK_INPUTS
pointing at that cache. The 
make dist
archive, the Debian source package and the 
.nosrc.rpm
contain no NVIDIA archives or generated firmware.

The packages put 

gpu_unlock
and its firmware in the initramfs and load it there, before 
nvidia
can bind a card:

  • mkinitcpio: 
    /etc/mkinitcpio.conf.d/zz-gpu-unlock.conf
    inserts 
    gpu_unlock
    right before 
    nvidia
    in 
    MODULES
    , so a display card is blank for as short a time as possible. Without 
    nvidia
    in the image, it goes last and still runs before an 
    nvidia
    loaded from the root filesystem. Images are rebuilt on install. mkinitcpio ignores drop-ins for an image built with 
    -c <config>
    or a preset 
    _config
    ; put 
    gpu_unlock
    right before 
    nvidia
    in that config's 
    MODULES
    yourself.
  • initramfs-tools: 
    /usr/share/initramfs-tools/modules.d/gpu-unlock.conf
    .
  • dracut: 
    /usr/lib/dracut/dracut.conf.d/gpu-unlock.conf
    .

With initramfs-tools and dracut, the module is built for every installed kernel that has headers, and those kernels' images are rebuilt on install and again on removal. Kernels installed later get the module and a new image from the kernel's own install hooks.

There is no 

softdep nvidia pre:
rule: kmod honours only the first 
softdep nvidia
line it reads, so other packages' rules (
nvidia-utils
, 
gddr6_hwmon
) would silently override it, or it would override theirs.

The module does nothing unless the kernel command line opts in:

      
gpu_unlock.targets=all                          # every unbound GA102/GA103/GA104/GA106 card
gpu_unlock.targets=0000:21:00.0                 # only these cards
gpu_unlock.targets=0000:21:00.0,0000:22:00.0    # comma-separated

Addresses are full PCI names as 

lspci -D
prints them (hex digits in either case), independent of GPU numbering and display role. An entry that is not a GA102/GA103/GA104/GA106 card, including 
all
mixed with addresses, is logged and ignored. The cards are unlocked concurrently, about a second in all however many there are, and each on its own: a card that is already bound or powered down is skipped. Bus mastering that the board firmware left on (Supermicro X11 does this whatever its option ROM and bus master settings) is cleared first; a card some driver already initialised is still refused. Then 
nvidia
loads and binds every card as usual.

The display card works too. Its firmware framebuffer (the boot console and Plymouth) keeps running while the unlock's firmware steps run, and is removed just before the card's reset, as 

nvidia-drm
would do a moment later anyway. Its screen is blank from that reset until 
nvidia-drm
takes over.

Loading the module by hand after boot does nothing to a card that 

nvidia
has bound.

Suspend to RAM powers the cards off, which resets the speed selectors. After resume the module unlocks every card it unlocked at boot again, before 

nvidia
resumes it: its suspend notifier runs just ahead of the one 
nvidia
resumes its cards from (
NVreg_UseKernelSuspendNotifiers=1
, the default in current drivers; 
nvidia-resume.service
runs later still). This adds about a second to resume. A card that kept power, as in suspend to idle, is still unlocked and is only read. A card that 
nvidia
has already resumed, or that is bound to another driver, is left as it is, and the log says why. Add 
gpu_unlock.resume=0
to the kernel command line, or write 
0
to 
/sys/module/gpu_unlock/parameters/resume
, to turn this off. Hibernation is not covered.

Check the result with:

journalctl -k -b | grep gpu_unlock
lspci -nnk -s 0000:21:00.0

To stop unlocking, remove 

gpu_unlock.targets=
from the kernel command line; for a one-off boot, delete it in the bootloader's edit screen. Removing the packages also removes the module and the initramfs drop-ins.

If the firmware on a card never stops, the module logs it and keeps the DMA buffers that firmware may still use until the next power off. Power off before trying again.

The kernel module and local packaging are GPL-2.0-only. The generated payload derives from the pinned CMP reference; NVIDIA firmware remains under its own terms. See 

firmware/NOTICE.md
and 
licenses/
for attribution and notices.

[#15](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/15),

[#33](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/33)), diffusion and

```

cd gpu-unlock

existing options:

- **GRUB (Debian/Ubuntu/Mint):** add it inside `GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT` in `/etc/default/grub`, then run `sudo update-grub`.
- **GRUB (Arch/CachyOS):** same edit, then run `sudo grub-mkconfig -o /boot/grub/grub.cfg`.
- **Fedora/RHEL:** run `sudo grubby --update-kernel=ALL --args="gpu_unlock.targets=all"`.

(`bootctl status` shows its location).

```

For other distributions, select a compatible explicit target above.

`make arch`, `make deb` and `make rpm` only build. Debian and RPM packages go

`~/.cache/gpu-unlock/inputs` (`make inputs`; override with `INPUTS=`).

The packages put `gpu_unlock` and its firmware in the initramfs and load it
there, before `nvidia` can bind a card:

- **mkinitcpio:** `/etc/mkinitcpio.conf.d/zz-gpu-unlock.conf` inserts `gpu_unlock` right before `nvidia` in `MODULES`, so a display card is blank
for as short a time as possible. Without `nvidia` in the image, it goes
last and still runs before an `nvidia` loaded from the root filesystem.
Images are rebuilt on install. mkinitcpio ignores drop-ins for an image
built with `-c <config>` or a preset `_config`; put `gpu_unlock` right
before `nvidia` in that config's `MODULES` yourself.
- **initramfs-tools:** `/usr/share/initramfs-tools/modules.d/gpu-unlock.conf`.
- **dracut:** `/usr/lib/dracut/dracut.conf.d/gpu-unlock.conf`.

With initramfs-tools and dracut, the module is built for every installed kernel that has headers, and those kernels' images are rebuilt on install and again on removal. Kernels installed later get the module and a new image from the kernel's own install hooks.

There is no `softdep nvidia pre:` rule: kmod honours only the first
`softdep nvidia` line it reads, so other packages' rules (`nvidia-utils`,
`gddr6_hwmon`) would silently override it, or it would override theirs.

The module does nothing unless the kernel command line opts in:

```
gpu_unlock.targets=all                          # every unbound GA102/GA103/GA104/GA106 card
gpu_unlock.targets=0000:21:00.0                 # only these cards
gpu_unlock.targets=0000:21:00.0,0000:22:00.0    # comma-separated
```

case), independent of GPU numbering and display role. An entry that is not
a GA102/GA103/GA104/GA106 card, including `all` mixed with addresses, is logged and ignored.
The cards are unlocked concurrently, about a second in all however many
there are, and each on its own: a card that is already bound or powered
down is skipped. Bus mastering that the board firmware left on (Supermicro
X11 does this whatever its option ROM and bus master settings) is cleared

The display card works too. Its firmware framebuffer (the boot console and
Plymouth) keeps running while the unlock's firmware steps run, and is

Loading the module by hand after boot does nothing to a card that `nvidia`

`/sys/module/gpu_unlock/parameters/resume`, to turn this off. Hibernation is
not covered.

Check the result with:

```
journalctl -k -b | grep gpu_unlock
lspci -nnk -s 0000:21:00.0
```
To stop unlocking, remove `gpu_unlock.targets=` from the kernel command line;
for a one-off boot, delete it in the bootloader's edit screen. Removing the
packages also removes the module and the initramfs drop-ins.

If the firmware on a card never stops, the module logs it and keeps the DMA buffers that firmware may still use until the next power off. Power off before trying again.

The kernel module and local packaging are GPL-2.0-only. The generated payload

使用 initramfs-tools 和 dracut，该模块是为每个已安装的具有标头的内核构建的，并且这些内核的映像在安装时重新构建，并在删除时再次构建。稍后安装的内核会从内核自己的安装挂钩中获取模块和新映像。

没有

softdep nvidia pre:
规则：kmod 仅尊重第一个
softdep nvidia
它读取的行，所以其他包的规则（
nvidia-utils
, 
gddr6_hwmon
）会默默地覆盖它，或者它会覆盖他们的。

除非内核命令行选择加入，否则该模块不会执行任何操作：

      
gpu_unlock.targets=all                          # every unbound GA102/GA103/GA104/GA106 card
gpu_unlock.targets=0000:21:00.0                 # only these cards
gpu_unlock.targets=0000:21:00.0,0000:22:00.0    # comma-separated

地址是完整的 PCI 名称，如下所示

lspci -D
打印它们（无论哪种情况都是十六进制数字），与 GPU 编号和显示角色无关。非 GA102/GA103/GA104/GA106 卡的参赛作品，包括
all
与地址混合，被记录并被忽略。这些卡同时解锁，无论有多少张卡，总共大约一秒钟，并且每张卡都是独立的：跳过已经绑定或断电的卡。首先清除主板固件保留的总线主控（无论其选项 ROM 和总线主控设置如何，Supermicro X11 都会执行此操作）；一些驱动程序已经初始化的卡仍然被拒绝。然后
nvidia
像往常一样加载并绑定每张卡。

显卡也能用。其固件帧缓冲区（启动控制台和普利茅斯）在解锁固件步骤运行时保持运行，并在卡重置之前被删除，如下所示

nvidia-drm
无论如何，稍后会做。从重置开始，它的屏幕是空白的，直到
nvidia-drm
接管。

启动后手动加载模块对卡没有任何作用

nvidia
已绑定。

挂起至 RAM 会关闭卡电源，从而重置速度选择器。恢复后，模块会再次解锁启动时解锁的每张卡，之前

nvidia
恢复它：它的挂起通知程序在之前运行
nvidia
从 (
NVreg_UseKernelSuspendNotifiers=1
，当前驱动程序中的默认值；
nvidia-resume.service
仍然运行得更晚）。这会增加大约一秒钟的恢复时间。保持电源状态的卡（如处于挂起状态至空闲状态）仍处于解锁状态并且只能读取。一张卡
nvidia
已经恢复，或者绑定到另一个驱动程序，保持原样，日志说明原因。添加
gpu_unlock.resume=0
到内核​​命令行，或者写入
0
到
/sys/module/gpu_unlock/parameters/resume
，将其关闭。休眠不包括在内。

检查结果：

journalctl -k -b | grep gpu_unlock
lspci -nnk -s 0000:21:00.0

要停止解锁，请删除

gpu_unlock.targets=
从内核命令行；对于一次性启动，请在引导加载程序的编辑屏幕中将其删除。删除软件包也会删除模块和 initramfs 插件。

如果卡上的固件从未停止，模块会记录它并保留固件可能仍使用的 DMA 缓冲区，直到下次断电为止。重试之前请先关闭电源。
